cited_evidence: job_1 assemble_provenance source appends {'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), ...}, substituting source_id into record_id.
job_2 input needs contains record_id values n06-r01 through n06-r08, while job_2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01 through s08.
handoffs for needs and evidence_sources show matching producer_sha256 and consumer_sha256, so downstream consumed the upstream outputs exactly.
observed job_2 priorities show upstream_rank: 0 for every record, demonstrating the provenance ranks were not matched to need record identities.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution contains a provenance identity fault in the upstream job. The needs handoff preserves need record_ids n06-r01 through n06-r08, but the evidence_sources handoff uses source ids s01 through s08 in its record_id field. Because the controller recorded exact hash handoffs, job_2 consumed that faulty upstream artifact exactly. Downstream prioritization then could not match evidence_sources.record_id to coverage.record_id, producing upstream_rank 0 for every priority instead of preserving upstream provenance rank.
